summary.text:
The user wants me to act as a skeptical-reader judge and return a JSON result comparing the BOOK ENTRY for "Wall" against the common interpretation and evidence.
{
  "verdict": "PERSUADED",
  "core_support": "FULL",
  "unsupported_glossary_assertions": [],
  "chapter_only_objections": [],
  "strongest_counter": "The wall primarily symbolizes divine protection and security, with the dividing-wall and false-security senses as prominent alternatives (Responses B and C). The book narrows the primary meaning to 'salvation = the covenant's enclosure' and treats self-built walls as counterfeits, but the supplied texts do not exclude the broader protective reading; they simply highlight two specific poetic applications.",
  "comparison": "The book entry's core identification — wall as Salvation, the covenant's enclosure, with God as wall of fire — is directly grounded in the exact verses cited (Isa 60:18; Zech 2:5). The counterfeits (Prov 18:11; Ezek 13) are also verbatim. While common interpretations treat 'protection security  salvation' as the default, the book's definitional phrasing ('thou shalt call thy walls Salvation') and explicit contrast with self-built walls align more tightly with the printed references than the broader symbolic lists in Responses A–D. The entry therefore supplies the best-supported explanation of the supplied scriptural evidence.

content.text:
{
  "persuasion": "PERSUADED",
  "support_scope": "FULL",
  "rationale": "The four printed texts directly establish the entry’s claims: Isaiah 60:18 names walls Salvation; Zechariah 2:5 identifies God Himself as the enclosing wall of fire; Proverbs 18:11 and Ezekiel 13:10–15 supply the self-built counterfeits (wealth’s high wall in conceit; the whitewashed wall of false peace destroyed by storm). No material assertion printed in the glossary entry lacks textual support. The strongest common reading (polyvalent protection/security) is broader and less precise; it does not displace the entry’s tighter identification of wall as salvation/covenant enclosure plus the named counterfeits, which the cited verses themselves carry.",
  "book_core_identification": "Wall = Salvation, the covenant’s enclosure (God Himself round about His people).",
  "book_secondary_elaborations": [
    "The counterfeit wall is self-built",
    "Wealth’s high wall “in his own conceit” (Prov 18:11)",
    "The whitewashed wall of false peace that the storm flattens (Ezek 13:10–15)"
  ],
  "unsupported_glossary_assertions": [],
  "chapter_only_objections": [
    "Chapter application of wall-removal as withdrawal of salvation in the vineyard sentence (Isa 5:5) and AD 70 fulfillment",
    "Chapter linkage of the vineyard hedge/phragmos to Ephesians 2’s middle wall of partition and one-way opening for Gentiles",
    "Chapter identification of tower, winepress, tenants, and rejected stone as extended vineyard symbolism beyond the glossary entry",
    "Chapter claim that salvation’s boundary was opened rather than abolished"
  ],
  "strongest_counter_interpretation": "Wall is a polyvalent image whose default sense is physical fortification extended metaphorically to protection, security, and divine safeguarding in general; ‘salvation’ is one poetic application (Isa 26:1; 60:18; Zech 2:5) among several common senses (dividing hostility, obstacle, self-control, judgment, false security), not a fixed definition that wall equals the covenant’s enclosure.",
  "counter_core_identification": "Protection, security, and divine safeguarding (context-dependent metaphor from city fortification).",
  "counter_relation_to_book_core": "SAME_CORE_BROADER",
  "material_core_denial": "The counter does not deny that walls can be called Salvation or that God can be a wall of fire; it denies that those texts fix ‘wall’ as definitionally ‘Salvation—the covenant’s enclosure’ rather than one instance of a broader protection/security figure.",
  "counter_case": [
    "Ancient walled cities make protection/security the natural base metaphor across many passages",
    "Ephesians 2:14, Jericho, Proverbs 25:28, Song 8:9–10, and judgment texts show other prominent senses",
    "Isaiah 60:18 and Zechariah 2:5 can be read as poetic naming of protective function rather than a uniform symbolic definition",
    "No single verse states ‘wall always means covenant enclosure’"
  ],
  "book_explanatory_advantages": [
    "Uses the exact wording of Isaiah 60:18 (‘call thy walls Salvation’) and Zechariah 2:5 (God as wall of fire) as definitional rather than loose illustration",
    "Unifies the positive figure with the two counterfeits printed in the same reference set (Prov 18:11; Ezek 13)",
    "Accounts for enclosure/boundary language (inside vs. outside) already present in the salvation and fire-wall texts",
    "Requires fewer extra assumptions than a free-floating ‘polyvalent protection’ label when restricted to the entry’s own cited witnesses"
  ],
  "counter_explanatory_advantages": [
    "Accommodates the full range of biblical wall uses without forcing every occurrence under ‘salvation/enclosure’",
    "Matches dictionary- and preaching-level defaults that list protection first and other senses as passage-specific"
  ],
  "evidence_book_core_cannot_explain": [],
  "comparative_winner": "BOOK",
  "decisive_sources": [
    "Isaiah 60:18",
    "Zechariah 2:5",
    "Proverbs 18:11",
    "Ezekiel 13:10–15"
  ],
  "unresolved_objections": [
    "Whether ‘covenant’s enclosure’ is the only legitimate paraphrase of the salvation/fire-wall texts, or merely a strong one among near-equivalents"
  ],
  "confidence": "high"
}

support_scope.description: Support for the exact glossary BOOK ENTRY only, never for the supporting chapter as a whole.

book_secondary_elaborations.description: Secondary assertions actually printed in the glossary BOOK ENTRY; exclude chapter-only claims.

unsupported_glossary_assertions.description: Material assertions actually printed in the BOOK ENTRY that the evidence does not support. Must be empty for FULL and nonempty for CORE_ONLY.

chapter_only_objections.description: Objections to applications or arguments found only in the supporting chapter. Preserved for later chapter review and excluded from the glossary scope ruling.

instructions: Return only the requested structured result. Judge the exact glossary entry against the strongest specific alternative; treat the chapter as evidence, not as an additional judgment target.
